extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing, processing, and deciding inter partes reexamination requests and for conduct of the resulting reexamination proceeding at the USPTO (CRU/IFW/PALM procedures, filing/processing rules, assignment, fees, and decision standards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing and hand-delivery address and Mail Stop marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence should be directed to the Customer Service Window, Randolph Building, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA 22314 and hand-carried correspondence and correspondence submitted by delivery service should be marked 'Mail Stop — Inter Partes Reexam.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended that the Mail Stop information be placed in a prominent position on the first page of each paper being filed utilizing a sufficiently large font size to direct attention to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fax for initial reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for inter partes reexamination may not be sent by facsimile transmission (FAX). See 37 CFR 1.6(d)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corrected/completed request sent in response to a notice that the original request was not filing date compliant also may not be faxed because it stands in place of or completes the original request. All subsequent inter partes reexamination correspondence, however, may be faxed to the Central Reexamination Unit at (571) 273-9900.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web submission permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for reexamination and reexamination 'follow-on' papers are permitted to be submitted using the Office's Web-based electronic filing system (EFS-Web).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Legal Framework for EFS-Web (www.uspto.gov/ebc/portal/efs/legal.htm) for rules and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of proceeding in correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing the request for reexamination, any letters sent to the Office relating to the reexamination proceeding should identify the proceeding by the number of the patent undergoing reexamination, the reexamination request control number assigned, the name of the examiner, and the examiner’s Art Unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing/transmission and Priority Mail Express use
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing and transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) and the Priority Mail Express® mailing procedure (37 CFR 1.10) may be used to file any paper in an inter partes reexamination proceeding except for a request for reexamination and a corrected/replacement request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 512 for certificate of mailing/transmission and MPEP § 513 for Priority Mail Express procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications directed to correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications from the Office to the patent owner will be directed to the correspondence address for the patent being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.33(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for amendments and papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed on behalf of patent owners must be signed by the patent owners, or the registered attorney or agent of record in the patent file, or any registered attorney or agent acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34.

rubrics_metrics.name: No routine double correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Double correspondence with the patent owners and the attorney or agent normally will not be undertaken by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no correspondence address is otherwise specified, correspondence will be with the most recent attorney or agent made of record by the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized papers will not be considered (37 CFR 1.939)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unauthorized paper is filed by any party at any time during the inter partes reexamination proceeding it will not be considered and may be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise authorized, no paper shall be filed prior to the initial Office action on the merits of the reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of prior art citations (37 CFR 1.902)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations by the patent owner in accordance with § 1.933 and by an inter partes reexamination third party requester under § 1.915 or § 1.948 will be entered in the inter partes reexamination file. Entry of other citations submitted after the order for reexamination by persons other than the patent owner or third-party requester will be delayed until the reexamination proceeding has been concluded by issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.502 for processing of prior art citations in ex parte reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted papers prior to first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for inter partes reexamination, no papers directed to the merits of the reexamination other than (A) citations of patents or printed publications under 37 CFR 1.501 and 1.933, (B) another complete request under 37 CFR 1.510, or (C) notifications pursuant to MPEP § 2686, should be filed prior to the date of the first Office action in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other papers directed to the merits filed prior to the first Office action will be returned to the sender without consideration; if entered prior to discovery of impropriety they will be expunged from the record. A copy of the notification of returned/expunged papers will be made of record, but the Office will not retain a copy of the returned/expunged papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and certified copies of reexamination files
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a 'certified copy' of a reexamination file, a CD-ROM may be purchased from the Document Services Division of OPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies may also be ordered from Document Services or obtained from IFW via PAIR; orders must indicate the reexamination control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reexamination files via Public PAIR
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination files are open to inspection by the general public by way of the Public PAIR via the USPTO Internet site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When viewing images of reexamination proceedings, the public can view the entire content of the reexamination file with the exception of non-patent literature. To access Public PAIR go to www.uspto.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM and IFW record-keeping and search procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The PALM system and IFW are used to support and view reexamination proceedings; PALM provides continuity data (including reexamination number) and IFW provides access to papers of a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the USPTO intranet click 'PALM' then 'General Information', enter the patent number, click 'Search', then 'Continuity Data' to obtain the reexamination number. There is typically about a ten (10) day lag between filing and data entry into PALM. If patent files are paper they should be ordered and scanned into IFW.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM event reporting and status reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Major examination events for reexamination proceedings must be reported in PALM (e.g., determination mailed - denial/grant, petitions received, examiner actions mailed, owner responses, third-party comments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These events will be permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' portion of PALM; weekly reports can be generated to assure processing with 'special dispatch'. CRU Technical Support Staff is responsible for reporting events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee processing and applicable fees
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees in an inter partes reexamination proceeding are processed by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) and posted via the Revenue Accounting and Managing (RAM) program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees include the request fee (37 CFR 1.915(a)), fees for addition of claims by the patent owner (excess claims under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3)-(c)(4)), extension of time fees (37 CFR 1.956), appeal/brief/oral hearing fees (37 CFR 41.20(b)), and petition fees (37 CFR 1.937(d)). No fee is required for issuance of a reexamination certificate. Micro entity reductions are available to patent owners only for certain fees; small entity reductions are available to third party requesters for some fees but micro reductions are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of reexamination proceedings to CRU and examiner selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for design patents, reexamination requests are assigned to the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) art unit which examines the technology in which the patent is currently classified; the Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS) assigns the request to a primary examiner who is most familiar with the claimed subject matter and different from the original examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy is to avoid assignment to an examiner who participated in prior examination of the patent or parent application; exceptions allowed where original examiner is the only knowledgeable examiner but require CRU Director approval which must be stated in the decision on the request. If an earlier reexamination is still ongoing, the same examiner may be assigned the new reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling copending reissue and reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is pending and a reexamination request is filed (or vice versa), possible merger will be considered and assignment adjusted accordingly; merged proceedings are generally assigned to the examiner who would ordinarily handle the reissue application unless that examiner was involved in earlier examination of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPLA should be notified promptly for consideration of merger; if proceedings are merged, the merged proceeding assignment follows reissue handling rules. If reexamination has been ordered, first Office action will not accompany the order granting reexamination; notify OPLA and hand-deliver paper files to OPLA if in paper form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for inadvertent assignment to an original examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination is inadvertently assigned to an 'original examiner' (and CRU/TC Director approval is not stated in the decision), the patent owner or third party requester who objects must promptly file a paper alerting the Office of this fact within two months of the first Office action or other Office communication indicating the examiner assignment, or reassignment will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassignment will be addressed case-by-case. Assignment to the original examiner alone is not grounds to vacate Office decisions or restart the reexamination. In some cases the Office may waive rules to enter and consider a paper directed to examiner assignment even if it otherwise lacks right of entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time reporting for reexamination activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO personnel should report all time spent on reexamination on their individual Time and Attendance Reports, including supervision, copying, typing, and docketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate reporting of time expended on reexamination activities is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/examiner decision standard and timing (35 U.S.C. 312 / 37 CFR 1.923)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than 3 months after filing of a request for inter partes reexamination, the Director (or examiner) must determine whether a 'substantial new question of patentability' is raised (for requests filed prior to September 16, 2011) or whether the request shows a 'reasonable likelihood that the requester would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged' (for requests filed between September 16, 2011 and September 15, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination is based on the claims in effect at the time, becomes part of the official file, is mailed to patent owner and requester, is final and non-appealable, and may result in a partial refund of the request fee if reexamination is not ordered (37 CFR 1.925). No input from the patent owner is considered prior to the determination. The decision's main object is granting or denying reexamination; ultimate patentability is decided later during the examination stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for litigation search prior to determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making a determination on the request for reexamination, a litigation search from TSS (CRU) or STIC must be done to check if the patent has been, or is, involved in litigation; a copy of the litigation search is scanned into IFW reexamination file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is or was involved in litigation and a paper referring to the court proceeding has been filed, reference to the paper by number should be made in the 'Litigation Review' box of the IFW file jacket form. If litigation has concluded or is taking place, the request must be promptly brought to the attention of the examiner's CRU SPRS for review for conformance to current Office litigation policy and guidelines (see MPEP § 2686.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of claims considered in decision and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on the request should discuss all of the patent claims requested for reexamination; the Office's determination and reexamination will generally be limited to the claims for which reexamination was requested and the requester must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim requested (35 U.S.C. 311(b)(2) and 37 CFR 1.915(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, those claims are not statutorily entitled to reexamination and will generally not be reexamined. If a request fails to set forth pertinency and manner for any claim, a filing date will not be awarded to the request. The Office may, in its discretion, reexamine claims not requested or initiate reexamination on its own (35 U.S.C. 303(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-claim sufficiency for granting reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: It is only necessary to establish that a substantial new question of patentability or a reasonable likelihood that the requester will prevail exists as to one of the patent claims in order to grant reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No prima facie case of unpatentability need be found to grant an order for reexamination; the examination stage will determine ultimate patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should not reject claims in the order for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner SHOULD NOT reject claims in the order for reexamination; any rejection of the claims will be made in the first Office action that normally will accompany the order for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2660 for first Office action practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds and petitions after refusal to order reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where inter partes reexamination is not ordered, a refund of a portion of the fee for requesting inter partes reexamination will be made in accordance with § 1.26(c) (37 CFR 1.925). The third party requester may seek review by a petition to the Director under § 1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner's determination refusing to order inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.927).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no petition is timely filed or if the decision on petition affirms refusal, the determination is final and nonappealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reissue on reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for reexamination is filed on a patent after a reissue patent for that patent has already issued, reexamination will be denied because the patent on which the request is based has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination of the reissued patent is desired, a new request for reexamination, including and based on the specification and claims of the reissue patent, must be filed. If the reissue issues after the filing of a request for reexamination, see MPEP § 2686.03.
